title: Labels, IDs and the ID stack
description:
Implement ImGui's label rules with a simpler hash. ImGui really uses a CRC32-based hash; here use **FNV-1a**, which is short to write:

```
hash = seed XOR 2166136261         (both 32-bit unsigned)
for each byte b of the text:  hash = (hash XOR b) * 16777619   (wrapping 32-bit arithmetic)
```

Write

```cpp
std::string displayText(const std::string& label);                 // what the widget shows
std::string idText(const std::string& label);                      // the part of the label that is hashed
uint32_t hashText(const std::string& text, uint32_t seed);

class IdStack
{
public:
    explicit IdStack(uint32_t windowSeed);
    void push(const std::string& text);    // like PushID(text): the new seed is hashText(text, current seed)
    void push(int n);                      // like PushID(int): the same as push(std::to_string(n))
    void pop();                            // never pops the window's seed
    uint32_t idOf(const std::string& label) const;   // hashText(idText(label), current seed)
};
```

The label rules:

| Label | `displayText` | `idText` |
|---|---|---|
| `"Delete"` | `Delete` | `Delete` |
| `"Delete##3"` | `Delete` | `Delete##3` |
| `"##speed"` | (empty) | `##speed` |
| `"HP: 87###hp"` | `HP: 87` | `###hp` |

`displayText` is everything before the first `##` (which also covers `###`). `idText` is the whole label, unless it contains `###`: then it is the part from the first `###` to the end.
hints: Keep the stack as a `std::vector<uint32_t>` that starts with the window's seed. `push` hashes with the current top as the seed and pushes the result.
